title: Senate Budget Committee Votes 11–10 to Advance $71.7B ICE/CBP Reconciliation Package to Senate Floor — Full Floor Vote Imminent as Trump's June 1 Deadline Approaches
detail: On May 20, 2026, the Senate Budget Committee voted 11–10 along strict party lines to report the combined $71.7 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation package to the full Senate floor, clearing the final procedural hurdle before floor consideration. The package combines the Senate Judiciary Committee's $39.2 billion title (ICE hiring, 100,000+ detention beds, deportation infrastructure, 287(g) funding, immigration court operations) with the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee's (HSGAC) $32.5 billion title (CBP staffing, border wall, DHS technology and personnel). Senate Republicans had rewritten provisions struck earlier by the Senate Parliamentarian under the Byrd Rule — including the $1 billion White House ballroom security line and major border patrol/DHS appropriations sections — and the revised package was cleared for floor consideration. Senate Majority Leader John Thune announced a floor vote would occur later in the week to meet President Trump's June 1 signing deadline. The bill passed the House 215–211 on April 30 with zero Democratic support. Senate Democrats — who have systematically challenged each provision under the Byrd Rule — vowed to continue their challenges during floor consideration, including through a 'vote-a-rama' amendment process. The $71.7B package would represent the largest single-year immigration enforcement investment in U.S. history, roughly eight times ICE's FY2024 base budget of $9.1 billion. ICE detention currently stands at a record 73,000+. The package contains no independent oversight provisions, no use-of-force standards, and no minimum medical care requirements despite 30+ FY2026 deaths in ICE custody.

title: DHS Weekly Enforcement Release: ICE Arrests Murderers, Rapists, Drug Traffickers, and Other Criminal Noncitizens — Routine 'Making America Safe Again' Press Release Issued May 20
detail: On May 20, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security published its weekly 'Making America Safe Again' press release documenting ICE enforcement arrests of criminal noncitizens over the preceding week. The release highlighted arrests of individuals convicted of or charged with serious crimes including murder, sexual offenses, drug trafficking, and weapons violations. Acting Assistant Secretary Lauren Bis stated: 'Every day, our ICE law enforcement officers are out on the street arresting criminal illegal aliens.' The weekly press releases, issued routinely since January 2025, represent a core component of the Trump administration's public communications strategy on immigration enforcement, emphasizing arrests of individuals with serious criminal histories. Advocates and researchers note that the selective highlighting of criminal cases does not reflect the overall enforcement posture — TRAC Reports data shows that as of early 2026, approximately 70.8% of ICE detainees have no criminal conviction, and arrests of noncitizens without any criminal record have grown substantially under the current administration. ICE is conducting approximately 7,369 arrests per week as of late April 2026, down from peak surge levels but far above pre-2025 baselines.
